title: Two changes shipped together
source: Live calls to Token Factory (Nemotron-3.5 Lightning) with injected faults

evidence.claim: Within the incident window, the only factor that varies is retries (varies_in_incident_window=true), with a slope of 2.91s per retry, explaining 2.18s of the 2.09s observed mean latency rise (R²=0.97).
Stratified by retries and input tokens: incident requests with 0-1 retries have median latency 0.47s (similar to baseline 0.39s), while those with 1-2 retries jump to 2.5s and 2+ retries to 6.48s.
Retry distribution shifted: baseline had 0 retries for all 20 requests; incident has 50% with 0 retries, 25% with 1 retry, 25% with 2 retries, and median latency increases with retry count.
Concurrency remained constant (avg_concurrency=1 in both windows) and stratifying by concurrency shows no latency difference.

A deploy event increased retrieval top_k from 2 to 40 before the incident, causing average input tokens to rise from 213 to 3701, but this factor does not vary within the incident window and its effect is negligible (unexplained_s = -0.095s).

rejected_hypotheses.why_rejected: Prompt size increased but does not vary within the incident window; median latency for large prompts with 0 retries (0.47s) is near baseline (0.39s). The effect split attributes only -0.095s to unexplained factors, indicating prompt expansion is not the driver of the latency spike.
Average concurrency is 1 in both baseline and incident; stratified tables show identical concurrency buckets (0-2) with no latency separation.
Error rate is 0% in both windows; requests without retries exhibit normal latency (~0.47s), indicating the provider is not universally slowed.
The effect split model explains 97% of within-window variance and identifies retries as the sole varying factor; stratified tables confirm the retry–latency relationship.

uncertainties: Why retries increased is not directly observed (error rate 0%); could be client-side timeouts triggered by longer prompt processing, but no timeout telemetry is present.
recommended_actions: Audit client retry logic: determine retry conditions (e.g., latency thresholds, timeout settings) and add exponential backoff.
Correlate retry occurrence with prompt size to see if larger prompts cause longer first-token latency that triggers retries.
Consider reducing top_k or implementing prompt truncation to limit input token growth.
Add monitoring for retry reasons (timeout, 5xx, client-cancelled) to distinguish provider vs. client triggers.

result.method: latency ~ the factors that vary inside the incident window, fitted on the incident window only
result.note: A factor with varies_in_incident_window=false changed between the normal period and the incident but cannot be told apart from the other changes in this window; its effect is in 'unexplained_s' if it matters.
